milestones.description: Wrexham AFC finish the European International Cup group stage with a perfect record — wins over Mallorca (2-0), M'gladbach (2-0), and RCD Espanyol (3-0), the last capped by Leo Sauer's Man of the Match display.
Juan Cruz Vargas (17) loaned to Ipswich Town for the 2027-28 season, seeking senior development minutes away from Wrexham's crowded CAM options.

Wrexham AFC sign Gabonese striker Musa Tine (17) as a free agent, agreeing a 4-year deal worth $17,000/week plus a $175,000 signing bonus. The 68-rated forward gives the club a genuine young No. 9 option behind Obi while Yacel Amrizi continues his recovery from injury.

FA Community Shield final confirmed: Wrexham AFC (Premier League champions) vs Manchester City (FA Cup holders), Wembley Stadium, Saturday 7 August 2027, kickoff 5:00 PM — the club's first-ever Community Shield appearance.

Pre-season loan business: seven players sent out for 2027-28 development minutes, including academy graduates Stephane Bertrand (Carrarese Calcio, 1yr) and Nathan Salaun (Barnet, 2yr), both promoted to the senior squad and loaned out the same day. Also out: Fabricio Sandoval (Hull City, 2yr), Nico Kopp (FC Basel 1893, 1yr), Vittorio Martini (CD Castellon, 1yr), Matthieu Brunel (West Brom, 1yr), and Lilian Faure (Bristol City, 1yr).

Wrexham AFC sign Polish goalkeeper Adrian Kaczmarek (17) from Club Atlético Vélez Sarsfield for $12.7M, agreeing a 4-year deal at $6,200/week. Tagged 'World Class Prospect Goalkeeper' by the club's scouting network (Potential 84-90), he slots in as rotation depth behind Okonkwo and Klaverboer.

Pre-season loan business continues: Santiago Ortega loaned to Watford (1yr, 12 Jul), Emiliano Bianchi loaned to Jagiellonia (2yr, 14 Jul), and Bailey Cadamarteri loaned to Fulham (2yr, 15 Jul, after an initial loan proposal was rejected).

Premier League Team of the Season announced — no Wrexham player named, despite the club winning the title. XI: Donnarumma (GK); Mauro Jr, Gvardiol, Thiaw, Frimpong; B. Barcola, B. Fernandes, Traoré, Saka; Gyökeres, Haaland.
Squad update
Squad update — Yacel Amrizi back in first-team training, nearing full recovery from his torn quad injury (sustained 2027-05-15 vs Manchester City).
Youth Academy Rush Tournament: Wrexham beat Fulham 5-3 (QF) and Nottingham Forest 4-1 (SF) before losing the final 1-4 to Burnley, ending the academy's run of four straight titles.

Academy roster gap flagged: Knut Inge Pedersen is a real youth academy player not yet entered in youth_academy.csv. Awaiting screenshots to add his row (attributes, position, age, potential) -- do not confuse with Knut Inge Bakke, an existing academy player who also featured in the 2027-08-15 Youth Rush semi-final.

First defeat of the Premier League title defence: 0-3 away to Liverpool at Anfield, ending the perfect start (2W-0L). Wrexham drop to 6th (6 pts) but stay in a UEFA Conference League qualification spot.

Wrexham AFC play their first-ever UEFA Champions League match -- a 0-0 away draw at Inter Milan (shown in-game as "Lombardia FC") in the League Phase opener. A club that was playing National League football in 2020-21 now shares a European table with Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, and Barcelona. Jenkins rotated heavily, fielding a youth-led XI.

Deadline-day business: Lewis Miley signed from Newcastle United for $37,500,000 -- a club-record transfer fee. Milán Vitális (Ipswich Town, $7m) and Vladyslav Veleten sold to Getafe CF ($8m), and Musa Tine loaned to FC St. Pauli for two years.
Lewis Miley makes his Wrexham debut in a 2-1 win over Sunderland, rated 7.4 at CDM -- an immediate return on the club-record fee.
Academy prospects Knut Inge Bakke (18, RM) and Even Jensen (18, LB) promoted to the first team, both signing on as Prospects. Welsh centre-back Harry Bound (17, CB/CDM) joins the Youth Academy.

Wrexham beat Bolton 2-0 in the Carabao Cup third round at Racecourse II to reach Round 4, with academy graduates Knut Inge Bakke and Even Jensen making their senior debuts a week after their promotion.

Wrexham beat Newcastle United 1-0 at the Racecourse, Yacel Amrizi's 22nd-minute strike (assisted by Toni Fruk) enough to see off Lewis Miley's former club. The win moves Wrexham up to 5th on 12 points, back into a UEFA Europa League qualification spot.

Wrexham beat Legia Warszawa 3-1 in UEFA Champions League League Phase Matchday 2, Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Miley scoring either side of Legia's equalizer before Knut Inge Bakke -- promoted from the academy just 11 days earlier -- scored his first senior goal in stoppage time on his Champions League debut. Wrexham move to 9 points from two matches, inside the League Phase's knockout play-off positions.

Keeyvon Jenkins accepts an offer to become Head Coach of the United States Women's National Team, effective immediately, while remaining Wrexham AFC manager. The US Soccer Federation's contract is contingent on winning the Women's International Cup within 12 months. Jenkins becomes the first manager in Wrexham's history to hold a concurrent national-team post while in charge of the club.

Wrexham win 3-1 away at Brighton -- Lewis Miley, Yacel Amrizi, and Chido Obi on the scoresheet -- to move up to 2nd in the Premier League on 15 points, into the UEFA Champions League qualification places. It is the club's best league position since the title-winning 2026-27 season.

Wrexham lose 0-4 at home to Leeds United, the season's heaviest defeat -- Brian Gutiérrez, honoured with a pre-match tifo, was sent off for two bookable offences inside the first 28 minutes, leaving the side a man down for over an hour. Jenkins was visibly furious with the dismissal after the match. Wrexham drop to 4th but remain on 15 points.
